problems.title: Successive percentage increases
problems.question: Increase a positive number50%, then20%. Find the total increase.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: The final multiplier is 1.5·1.2=1.8.
steps: The added fraction is 1.8−1=0.8, so the increase is 80%.

problems.title: Two profit rates on the same cost
problems.question: A sale at 15% profit earns750 lari. How much would25% profit earn?
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Profit is the given percentage of the cost. Cost=750/0.15=5000.

problems.title: Cancel prime powers
problems.question: Evaluate 18⁷·12⁶/(24⁶·6⁵·9³).
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
steps: The remaining exponent of 2 is 7+12−18−5=−4; of 3 it is 14+6−6−5−6=3.
Thus the value is 3³/2⁴=27/16.

problems.title: Extend a median by its own length
problems.question: AD is a triangle median, DE=AD with A, D, E collinear. Given∠ACD=56°,∠ABD=40°, find∠ACE.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: D bisects both AE and BC, so ABEC is a parallelogram and CE∥AB.
steps: In ABC,∠A=180−56−40=84°. At C, the angle ACE is supplementary to∠A, so it is 96°.

problems.title: An angle equals a difference
problems.question: One triangle angle equals the difference of the other two. Find the largest angle.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Let A=B−C, with B>C. Then A+B+C=2B=180°.
steps: Therefore B=90°, and it is the largest angle.

problems.title: A weighted mean age
problems.question: 30 women average42 years,40 men average49. Find all 70 employees’ average age.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
steps: The total age is 3220, and 3220/70=46.

problems.title: Incentre angle of a right triangle
problems.question: A triangle has one angle equal to the sum of the other two, and C is largest. O is the incenter. Find∠AOB.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: C=90°. The incenter formula is∠AOB=90°+C/2.

problems.title: Compare quantities with linked ratios
problems.question: a:b=2:3, b:c=6:5, all positive. By what percentage is a less than c?
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Use a:b:c=4:6:5.
steps: The relative shortfall is(c−a)/c=(5−4)/5=20%.

problems.title: Perpendicular bisector in a30–60 triangle
problems.question: ABC is right at C,∠A=2∠B. The perpendicular bisector of AB meets BC at K. Find∠CKA.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: ∠B=30°,∠A=60°. Since KA=KB, triangle ABK has base angles at A and B both 30°.
steps: Thus∠AKB=120°. The ray KC is opposite KB, so∠CKA=60°.

problems.title: Conserve dry matter
problems.question: Fresh plums contain75% water, dried plums10%. How much fresh fruit gives 2.5kg dried?
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Dry matter stays constant. The dried fruit contains2.5·0.9=2.25kg dry matter.
steps: Fresh fruit is 25% dry matter, so its mass is 2.25/0.25=9kg.

problems.title: Solve then take a remainder
problems.question: Find the remainder modulo5 of the root of(4x−12)/3−7=x/6+10.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Multiply by 6:8x−24−42=x+60.
steps: Thus 7x=126, x=18, whose remainder modulo5 is 3.

problems.title: An altitude falls beyond an obtuse vertex
problems.question: Triangle angles A:B:C=2:6:1. Altitude CK meets line AB at K. Given AB=a, BK=b, find AK.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: The angles are 40°,120°,20°. Since B is obtuse, the altitude foot lies beyond B.
steps: The order is A, B, K, so AK=AB+BK=a+b.

problems.title: An identity in x
problems.question: For which a does2ax−5=10x−a have infinitely many roots?
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Both coefficients must agree:2a=10 and −5=−a.
steps: Both equations give a=5. Then the original equality holds for every x.

problems.title: Orthocentre angle
problems.question: In an acute triangle, B is the mean of A, C. O is the orthocentre. Find∠AOC.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: 2B=A+C and A+B+C=180°, so B=60°. The orthocentre angle is 180°−B.
steps: Thus∠AOC=120°.

problems.title: Last digits of nested powers
problems.question: Find the remainder modulo10 of(13⁸¹)⁵+(17¹⁰¹)⁴+22²²²².
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: The last digits are 3⁴⁰⁵,7⁴⁰⁴,2²²²². Their cycles have length 4.
steps: They end in3,1,4, respectively. The sum ends in8.

problems.title: A bisector perpendicular to a median
problems.question: BM is an angle bisector and CN is a median, with BM⊥CN. If AC=10 and perimeter ABC=31, find AB.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: In triangle BCN, the line BM bisects the angle between BC and BN and is perpendicular to CN. Hence BC=BN.
steps: Since N is midpoint AB, AB=2BC. The perimeter gives 3BC+10=31, so BC=7 and AB=14.

problems.title: Order does not affect multiplication
problems.question: Three results a, b, c come from applying+10%,−15%,+5% to the same x in different orders. Compare them.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Each result is x·1.1·0.85·1.05.
steps: Multiplication is commutative, so the order of these three fixed factors makes no difference.

problems.title: Two perpendicular bisectors
problems.question: Perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC meet AC at P, K, with A, P, K, C in order. If AC=12, find perimeter BPK.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: PA=PB and KB=KC.
steps: Perimeter BP+PK+KB=AP+PK+KC=AC=12.

problems.title: Divisors of a product of consecutive integers
problems.question: Find the number of positive divisors of 20·21·…·29.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: The prime factorization is 2⁹·3⁵·5³·7²·11·13·23·29. Divisor count=∏(exponent+1).

problems.title: Altitudes divided at the orthocentre
problems.question: Two altitudes meet inside a triangle. One is bisected; the other is divided2:1 from the vertex. Find∠C.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Write AD as the bisected altitude, BE as the other, and H as their intersection. Put AH=HD=t and BH=2HE. Similar right triangles AHE, BHD give AH·HD=BH·HE.
steps: Thus t²=BH²/2, so BH=√2t. In right triangle BHD, this forces BD=HD=t and∠HBD=45°.
Since AC⊥BH and BC⊥AD, the angle at C is 45°.

problems.title: Balance gold and silver
problems.question: Mix3 litres of 7:8 gold:silver alloy and 5 litres of 3:7 alloy. How much pure gold makes the amounts equal?
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
steps: Add the difference 5.1−2.9=2.2 litres of pure gold.

problems.title: An angle-bisector difference identity
problems.question: Triangle MNP has∠N=20°,∠P=40°, and angle bisector MK=5. Find NP−NM.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: ∠M=120°. Choose L on NP with NL=NM. Then triangle MNL has angles20°,80°,80°.
steps: Thus∠LMP=40°, so ML=LP. The bisector makes∠KML=20°, and because K lies between N, L, triangle MKL has other angles80°,80°. Hence MK=ML.
Therefore NP−NM=LP=ML=MK=5.

problems.title: Positive triples with a fixed range
problems.question: How many positive triples, ignoring order, have sum 26, largest−smallest14, and a pair in ratio2:3?
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Write sorted numbers u, v, u+14. Their sum gives v=12−2u, and the order requires0<u≤4.
steps: The ratios u:v=2:3 and v:(u+14)=2:3 give u=24/7 and u=1, respectively. They produce(24/7,36/7,122/7) and(1,10,15).
The remaining ratio u:(u+14)=2:3 gives u=28, which violates u≤4.
problems.note: The choices count triples up to rearrangement. If all ordered triples were counted separately, there would be 12.

problems.title: Replacing half a solution twice
problems.question: Two equal vessels start at 20% alcohol. First:replace half by alcohol, then half by water. Second:replace half by water, then half by alcohol. Find final alcohol ratio.
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: For a full vessel with alcohol fraction p, replacing half by alcohol gives(p+1)/2; by water gives p/2.
steps: The first fraction becomes0.2→0.6→0.3. The second becomes0.2→0.1→0.55.
Their ratio is 0.3/0.55=6/11.

problems.title: Distances and absolute-value ratios
problems.question: Two numbers are 14 apart and their magnitudes are in ratio3:4. How many pairs are possible?
problems.idea: Translate percentages into factors, or use equal triangles and exact arithmetic.
formulas: Write their magnitudes3t,4t, t>0. Same signs give t=14; opposite signs give7t=14, t=2.
steps: The pairs, with the smaller magnitude listed first, are(42,56),(−42,−56),(6,−8),(−6,8). There are 4.
